\section{External bona-fide captures (post hoc): does the operating point or the restoration cost transfer?}
\label{sec:s8}
These analyses (experiment records E069 and E070) were designed after the Track A results were known and use
public captures from other sensors: the FVC2000, FVC2002 and FVC2004 sets (Maltoni et al.) and NIST Special
Database 302 (the Nail to Nail Fingerprint Challenge; NIST TN 2007). They are post hoc external evidence, not
independent prospective validation. Only bona-fide captures are used: no synthetic image is generated for
these sensors, so only bona-fide rejection is measured. One $88\times88$ window per capture is taken about the
foreground centroid (both the 88 and 176 windows at least 80\,\% foreground); the Track A degradation
conditions and restoration operators are applied unchanged; every detector, normalization arm and threshold
$\tau_0$ is the frozen Track A one. Intervals are 95\,\% cluster-bootstrap intervals ($B=10{,}000$) with fingers
(FVC; no volunteer identifiers are released) or subjects (SD302; the same participants recur across devices)
as clusters, and devices are never pooled. Only aggregates are reported; no SD302 image or subject-level value is
redistributed.

\paragraph{The operating point does not transfer} At $\tau_0$, the frozen detectors reject degraded external
bona-fide windows at rates that differ from Track A's (1.1\,\%--1.9\,\%) by a median of
+0.069 (range -0.014 to +0.460); 123 of 168 device $\times$
detector $\times$ protocol $\times$ arm cells exceed twice the Track A rate (Table~\ref{tab:s_ext}).

\paragraph{The restoration cost transfers selectively} The preregistered rule asked whether the legacy-arm
increase in bona-fide rejection ($\Delta B>0$, interval excluding 0, under both protocol models) appears for at
least two of the three detector families, counting only cells whose degraded rejection lay in $[0.005,0.95]$.
It held on SD302 S for both operators and on SD302 M for TV only, and on no FVC
device; 7 of 14 devices had no interpretable reading for at least one operator,
mostly because protocol-2 legacy cells fell below the floor. The floor rule also removed cells in which
$\Delta B$ was resolved above zero; without it (not preregistered; descriptive) the rule would hold on
7 devices for bilateral and 8 for TV. The two pixel-domain detectors show the
Track A direction on most SD302 devices and two FVC sets, whereas D3's legacy $\Delta B$ is resolved below zero under both protocol models on
6 devices (bilateral) and 5 (TV): outside Track A, the sign of the
restoration effect on bona-fide rejection depends on the instrument and the device.

\paragraph{Capture quality: inconclusive} Among in-domain captures for NIST NFIQ~2 (v2.3.0; plain optical
captures at 500\,ppi with the ISO minimum area; 6 devices), the preregistered contrast (lowest minus
highest quality tertile of $\Delta B$, legacy arm) was not supported on any device. Only
FVC2000 DB3 had all three detector families eligible and adequate power, and 10 of its 11 resolved
contrasts (all arms and operators) pointed the other way (the high-quality tertile showed the larger change). The result is therefore
reported as inconclusive: no quality moderation was detected, which is not evidence of its absence.

\paragraph{Floor rule (audit)} The rule's floor excluded 20 of 168 cells, all protocol-2 cells
with degraded rejection below 0.005; 17 of them had $\Delta B$ resolved above zero under both operators
and none below zero. The rule was added on review, before any outcome was read; the rule-based counts therefore
understate the descriptive pattern, and the without-rule counts are a sensitivity analysis, not a registered result.

\section{A fingerprint-specific enhancer as the upstream transformation (post hoc)}
\label{sec:s9}
Experiment record E068 replaced the generic operators by FpEnhancer (Guan et al.; UNet variant, authors' weights,
MIT licence; \url{https://github.com/XiongjunGuan/FpEnhancer}), a learned enhancer whose output is a near-binary ridge map, applied to the degraded test and
validation images of both protocols and scored once by the frozen detectors and the matcher; it is post hoc and
is one enhancer, not an operator class, applied outside its training distribution (degraded crops rather than
rolled prints). The detector cells are the E049 instrument set (D3 and three ImageNet
backbones); the headline detectors are read separately below. All reproduction gates passed. Intervals are 95\,\% bootstrap intervals
over seeds, the 34 test subjects and synthetic images within generator ($B=10{,}000$).

\label{tab:s_enh}

At the frozen thresholds $\tau_0$ of the three headline detectors, bona-fide rejection of the 1,653 test reals fell
from 1.1--2.0\,\% to zero in all 12 detector $\times$ protocol $\times$ arm cells. At the
matcher's validation threshold (FMR $10^{-2}$), the single-template false non-match rate of enhanced probes
against clean templates rose from 0.613 to 0.995 (change +0.382, interval
+0.332 to +0.433). The detector shifts persisted under fixed normalization in all 8 cells
(primary readout $S_\mathrm{fix}=8/8$; E049 class B), AUC fell in 7 of 8 cells (to $-0.37$), and the per-image min--max
range was essentially unchanged (median ratio 1.00), consistent with a shift that does not run through per-image
normalization. Templates were not enhanced; an enhance-both pipeline
was not evaluated, and the lower synthetic detection rate is a measurement of this transformation, not an
evaluated attack.
